memory_candidates: lake exe checkInitImports failing with 'object file ... does not exist' is a downstream symptom, not a diagnosis: run lake build first and read the actual compile error, since a missing .olean is usually the consequence of a module that fails to elaborate rather than a stale build product.

literature-briefing.sh derives its chunk count from global-index entries whose parent_doc matches the doc_id, falling back to 1 when none exist - so a corpus can show 'chunk_count: 77' on its parent entry and 77 files on disk while the briefing renders '1 chunk(s)'. The per-repo specs/literature-index.json is reference-only and can never be the site of this defect.
